description: Acceptance vectors for a premium quote request, shared by the backend's QuoteRequestDto and the ML service's QuoteRequest. Both run every vector and must agree. Checking published field names and limits was not enough: a review found the two sides disagreeing on dates and on region whitespace while every schema-shape assertion passed. Calendar validity is included because shape agreement alone let both services accept dates that do not exist, in one case silently rolling them forward to a different day.

vectors.name: date with a time component
vectors.why: Coverage is measured in whole days. A time component has no meaning here and invites two readings of the same window, so both sides take dates only.

vectors.name: date without zero padding
vectors.why: One spelling per date keeps the window unambiguous.

vectors.name: single day window
vectors.why: Endpoints are inclusive, so this covers one day rather than none.

vectors.name: window past the on-chain maximum
vectors.why: MAX_DURATION_DAYS. A longer window could be priced but never created.

vectors.name: region with surrounding whitespace
vectors.why: Accepted, and preserved verbatim. The backend encodes the region into bytes32 as given, so trimming it in one service would quote a different region than the policy would carry.

vectors.name: region of only whitespace
vectors.why: Not a region. It used to pass the backend because IsNotEmpty only rejects the empty string, and would have been encoded on-chain as a bytes32 of spaces.

vectors.name: region at the byte budget
vectors.why: 31 bytes: the largest a bytes32 region code carries.

vectors.name: region one byte over the budget
multibyte region within the character count but over the byte budget
vectors.why: 16 characters, 32 UTF-8 bytes. The limit is a byte budget, not a length.

vectors.name: coverage with leading zeros
vectors.why: The shared amount pattern allows them; refusing would reject coverage the chain would insure.

vectors.name: coverage at the integer digit limit
vectors.why: Thirty integer digits.

vectors.name: coverage past the integer digit limit
coverage of zero written with decimals
coverage with nineteen decimals
vectors.why: Wei is the smallest unit; a nineteenth decimal cannot be represented.

vectors.name: threshold at the largest exactly representable integer
threshold past exact integer representation
vectors.why: Beyond 2^53 JavaScript silently changes the value, so a threshold that arrived corrupted must not be treated as merely large.

vectors.name: timestamp at midnight
vectors.why: Rejected even though it denotes the same day. Pydantic parsed it to a date while the backend refused it, so one spelling per date is the only way the two agree.

vectors.name: date that does not exist
vectors.why: Matches YYYY-MM-DD and is not a day. Worse than accepted, it was normalised: Date.parse rolls it to 2 March, so the window priced differed from the window requested.

vectors.name: month out of range
vectors.why: Parsed to NaN, which the range validators passed through on the assumption another check would catch it.

vectors.name: leap day in a leap year
vectors.why: 2028 is a leap year, so this is a real day and must be quotable.

vectors.name: leap day in a common year
vectors.why: 2026 is not a leap year.

vectors.name: end date that does not exist
vectors.why: Both endpoints are checked, not only the start.

vectors.name: coverage in Arabic-Indic digits
vectors.why: Python's digit class matches every Unicode decimal and int() parses them, so this validated and priced as 1 ETH while the backend refused it outright. JavaScript's digit class is ASCII-only.

vectors.name: coverage with a trailing newline
vectors.why: Python's end anchor also matches before a trailing newline, so this passed validation and then threw on conversion - a 500 for a malformed request. Matching the whole string closes it.

vectors.name: threshold as a boolean
vectors.why: bool subclasses int in Python and Number(true) is 1 in JavaScript, so true arrived as the threshold 1 on both - against an OpenAPI document that publishes an integer.

vectors.name: threshold in hexadecimal
vectors.why: Number() read it as 50 on the backend while the ML service refused it.

vectors.name: threshold as a decimal string
vectors.why: The one string form both accept: plain ASCII decimal digits.

vectors.name: date as a Unix timestamp
vectors.why: The backend takes text; a number reaching this field is a request the two services would answer differently.

vectors.name: region with an unpaired surrogate
vectors.why: Written as a literal escape rather than the character: a lone surrogate cannot be encoded to UTF-8, so a file containing one cannot be written. Both services must refuse it, and the ML service must refuse it as a 422 rather than failing to serialise the rejection.

vectors.name: date in the first century
vectors.why: Date.UTC maps years 0-99 onto 1900-1999, so the backend rejected these while the ML service accepted them. Setting the year explicitly keeps early years themselves.

vectors.name: year zero
vectors.why: Year zero exists in ISO 8601 and not in the proleptic Gregorian calendar Python uses, whose first year is 1. Accepted by the backend and refused by the ML service, so the contract had two readings.
